problem: Eighteen attacker findings, twelve blocking. Each question below carries my proposal as the recommended option; pick it, another, or write your own.

questions.text: Live trials versus the network ban and fc check rerunning every command at every gate. Who runs a trial and when?
questions.why: A model call is a network call; fc check reruns map commands at baseline, every gate and the stop gate.

options.value: Trials and judge runs happen once, outside the suite, and their records are committed; every suite is offline over records; C8 says a model call is made only by a trial, never by a suite.
The suite command starts the trial or judge itself each run; C8 exempts model calls.

questions.text: The mutation sweep would run the whole suite once per part inside run-all.
questions.why: Statistical and judged suites per mutation would be ruinous if live; offline they are cheap.

options.value: The sweep is one suite that runs the other suites' offline cases in a temporary copy, never a trial; parts with no meaningful mutation are exempt by an explicit list in the sweep's fixture.
The sweep is a separate command the reviewer runs once, outside run-all.

questions.text: Ratio denominator, inconclusive trials, and what groups scenarios into a set with a control.
questions.why: I3 has one folder per scenario and no set; a suite prints one ratio line.

options.value: Denominator is the declared N, inconclusive counts as not passing; a set is a folder of scenarios sharing one tier, with one ratio line per scenario.
Denominator is the conclusive count; one ratio line per suite.

questions.text: Who marks a trial inconclusive and where is it recorded?
questions.why: No record file carries a verdict today.

options.value: A fifth record file, verdict.txt, written by the deterministic check over the records.
The judge marks it in the sheet.

questions.text: A threshold tuned for opus implies pilot results, but C5 forbids deriving a threshold from results.

options.value: The threshold is fixed at authoring from the scenario's difficulty; C5 reads 'stated before the counted trials run'.
Allow a declared pilot of n trials whose results set the threshold, then the counted trials.

questions.text: Covers lines carry this spec's ids; the thirty old suites cite flightcrew-v1 ids, so continuity by id is meaningless.
questions.why: Continuity must be expressed as something both suites share.

options.value: Continuity of cases: every case name the thirty suites carry appears in the new suite, verbatim or under a committed mapping file; 'commands' dropped.
Drop B12 and E6; D5 already says the old suites are not a settled asset.

questions.text: The inventory has no listing rule, no granularity, no match rule.
questions.why: B1 and B2 both depend on it.

options.value: Inventory = MANIFEST.txt filtered to B1's categories; a runner command is a subcommand as fc's usage lists them; the .claude surface is what distribute writes; a case names a part by its repository-relative path or subcommand token in the case name.
Inventory = every file under flightdeck/flightcrew/ and .claude/; a case names a part by path only.

questions.text: MANIFEST.txt lists every existing suite file and must not change, so replacing a suite fails doctor and the manifest suite.
questions.why: Frozen thing versus the freedom SC1 gives.

options.value: Pin it as a defect; SC1 says suites are added and superseded, never deleted, until the refactor.
Allow MANIFEST.txt to change in this launch as the one exception to SC4.

questions.text: fc doctor expects agents under .claude/agents/flightcrew/; they sit at the top level; C10 is false as written.
questions.why: Cannot be made true without touching .claude.

options.value: C10 names only the hooks and settings; the agents location is pinned as a defect.
Move the agents into .claude/agents/flightcrew/ before the run as a setup act, like the fragment merge, and keep C10 whole.

questions.text: The v1 tooling expects the spec at flightdeck/launch/specs/<name>/ and pins that path; the draft lives in the new-layout folder.
questions.why: fc launch new will make a second folder and pin a path that does not exist.

options.value: Copy the frozen spec to flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-characterization/ before the run as its canonical home for the v1 tooling; name it in SC3 and the boundary; the new-layout folder keeps the interview.
Move the whole specs folder there and drop the new-layout folder for this launch.

questions.text: fc report re-renders report.md with a fixed heading list; a hand-added Defects section is dropped.
questions.why: The report is out of scope and unchanged.

options.value: The defect list is its own file, defects.md in the run's evidence folder, written by the run; I4 becomes that file.
Carry defects through fc launch note into the report's notes section.

questions.text: D6 calibrates the rubric with fable; C5 bans fable without exception.
questions.why: Calibration is your act, outside the run.

options.value: C5 reads 'no trial or judge run by the suite uses fable'; calibration with fable is yours and the human-graded examples are named as your input in SC3.
Calibrate on opus too; D6 drops 'with fable'.

questions.text: Rubrics, sheets and the judge model have no address.
questions.why: B8, B9 and E4 cannot be checked without one.

options.value: Rubric as rubric.md in the scenario set's folder; sheet as sheet.md under each trial folder; the judge model in the set's json.
Rubrics under flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/rubrics/<name>.md; sheets beside the suite's evidence.

questions.text: Defect lines cite a manual line, but schemas, templates, validators, gates and commands have no manual.
questions.why: A defect line needs a reference for every part.

options.value: Cite the part's own header comment or usage line where no manual exists.
Cite the tests-map check id instead.

questions.text: A sheet-level refusal (missing model, broken shape) has no question to name.

options.value: E3 names the question where there is one and the sheet path otherwise.
Split E3 into a question-level and a sheet-level edge.

questions.text: Where the meta-checks live, and the lock rule locks the suites the map names, so the builders could not write them.
questions.why: run-all would recurse if the run-all check is itself a suite.

options.value: Meta-checks are suites under an underscore-prefixed folder run-all skips, run only by the map's commands; locked paths name only those and the fixtures; allowed paths name the rest of testbench.
Meta-checks live outside testbench, under the run's launch folder as checks/.

questions.text: What a must or must_not string matches against.
questions.why: The deterministic check over records needs a rule.

options.value: A regular expression matched against the concatenated record files.
A tool name or hook decision matched against events.jsonl only.

questions.text: Session transcripts live outside the repository.
questions.why: The reviewer chooses one to read.

options.value: The run copies the reviewer's chosen transcript into the launch folder; SC3 says so.
Read in place outside the landing commit; SC3 says transcripts are not in the repository.
